question.text: The Ming dynasty was established after the Red Turban rebellions that overthrew this Chinese successor dynasty to the Mongol Empire. Marco Polo's writings about China were during the time of this dynasty.
question.answerHtml: Yuan Dynasty [do not accept or prompt on "Mongol Dynasty"]
question.clue: It ended when the Red Turban Rebellion forced Togon Temur to flee its capital of Dadu in 1368.

swap.leadin: During this rebellion, a Muslim group called the Hansu Braves set fire to Hanlin Academy during the Siege of the Foreign Legations.
swap.text: Name this rebellion which occurred during the Qing [Ching] dynasty and was defeated by the Eight-Nation Alliance.
swap.answerHtml: Boxer Rebellion [or Boxer Uprising; or other synonyms for “rebellion;” or Yihetuan Movement]
swap.clue: The International Legations were besieged during this conflict that arose out of resentment over unequal treaties such as those of Wangxia and Nanking.

question.leadin: A protest here led to Jeff Widener's iconic photograph of a man, possibly named Wang Weilin, standing in front of four tanks.
question.text: Name this Beijing square tragically cleared on the night of June 4, 1989 after Deng Xiaoping's conservative faction used their control of the military.
question.clue: In 1976, mass public displays of mourning at this site prompted disciplinary actions initiated by the Gang of Four.

swap.text: This military leader of the Kuomintang led the Northern Expedition at the start of the Chinese Civil War. He later led the Republic of China's exiled government on Taiwan.
swap.clue: This leader of the Northern Expedition was kidnapped by Zheng Xueliang in the Xi'an Incident.

question.leadin: While in exile in London, he was temporarily held prisoner in the Chinese embassy.
question.text: Name this Chinese revolutionary who proposed the Three Principles of the People, and founded both the Kuomintang and the Revere China Society.
question.clue: His party's ideals were expressed in works like the Five-Yuan Constitution and the Three Principles of the People.

swap.text: This Chinese leader, who was officially the chairman of the Central Military Commission at the time, was criticized for his crackdown against the protests. This person also replaced Zhao Ziyang with Jiang Zemin [j'yahng zuh-MIN] as General Secretary.
swap.clue: With Zhao Ziyang and Hu Yaobang, this man outmaneuvered Hua Guofeng for power.

question.text: The Silla Kingdom allied with this Chinese dynasty to conquer its neighbors. This dynasty was interrupted by Wu Zetian's short-lived Zhou Dynasty.
question.clue: This dynasty lost the battle of Talas to the Abbasids.

swap.text: This country performed its first nuclear test at Lop Nur, and later aided Pakistan in its nuclear program. The Cox Report accused it of stealing American weapons designs.
swap.clue: Ethnic minorities like the Uighurs were largely exempt from a famous policy in this country.

question.text: The anecdote about the Bai Qi (bye chee), "The Human Butcher," appears in this text by Sima Qian (suh-mah chee-EN), which claims that the Xia (sh'YAH) Dynasty were the first rulers in the lands that comprise modern-day China.
question.clue: This text describes the melting of thousands of enemy weapons to create twelve colossal metal statues, a loyalty test in which a man points to a deer and calls it a horse, and the "rectification of weights and measures."

swap.leadin: Name these famous women married to famous men.
swap.text: This third wife of Mao Zedong was a deputy leader of the Cultural Revolution before being ousted in 1976 as one of the Gang of Four.
swap.clue: This person was the main target of a protest that flouted a ban on mourning called the "Five Nos".

question.leadin: This woman died in the Hall of Graceful Bird, probably due to arsenic poisoning.
question.text: Name this woman who dominated the Qing Dynasty for over forty years. She was the mother of the Tongzhi Emperor and the aunt of the Guangxu Emperor. Either her name or her familiar title is okay.
question.answerHtml: Cixi [or Tzu-his, or the Dowager Empress, accept in reverse order]
question.clue: Despite later supporting the "New Policies," this ruler placed the Guangxu ("gwahng-shyoo") Emperor under house arrest after he launched the Hundred Days' Reform.

swap.leadin: These people built the Willow Palisade to seal off their homeland.
swap.text: Name this ethnic group that traditionally wore their hair in a single braid known as a "queue" and introduced the qipao ["CHEE-POW"] dress to China. The various tribes of this ethnic group were first united by Nurhaci ["noor-HAWCH-ee"].
swap.clue: This ethnic group forced the men they conquered to grow a ponytail called a queue.

question.leadin: A popular Han dynasty text was titled for the biographies of "virtuous" examples of these people.
question.text: Name these people, who were the subject of numerous "chastity arches" built during the Ming dynasty. These people were subjected to the painful practice of foot-binding.

swap.text: After passing the final Metropolitan Exam, candidates were awarded this highest and final degree. The purchasing of this degree toward the end of the Qing (ching) meant the "Imperial Scholars" who held it were no longer guaranteed the highest offices.
swap.clue: Successful candidates in the civil service exams were awarded this degree title. From the reign of the Ming emperor Yingzong ("EENG-DZONG"), only holders of this title were permitted into the Hanlin Academy.

question.leadin: This document was the first of a series of three similar announcements, and it included a pledge that neither party would "seek hegemony" in the Pacific region.
question.text: Identify this landmark diplomatic communique issued in 1972 from the namesake city that began the process of normalizing US-Chinese relations.
question.answerHtml: the Shanghai Communiqué [or the Joint Communiqué of the United States of America and the People’s Republic of China]

swap.leadin: The entire island province of Hainan is designated as one of these regions.
swap.text: Name these regions in China where restrictions on trade and investment are relaxed.
swap.clue: China had its own period of economic liberalization in the 1980s, setting up these administrative regions that relaxed the restrictions of the command economy. They include Zhuhai, Shantou, and Shenzen.

question.leadin: Opposed by conservative politicians like Su Dongpo, he came to prominence under Emperor Shenzong.
question.text: Name this great Chinese prime minister who promulgated the New Laws, initiating government loans to relieve peasants, established regional militias, and rewrote the civil examinations.
question.clue: This man created a financial bureau that raised officials' salaries while cutting the budget, instituted a 2-percent lending program for farmers through his "New Laws," and reformed the training of bureaucrats at the Hanlin Academy.

swap.text: The worship of Guan Yu became widespread in China because of this Ming dynasty novel, which details the rebellion of Guan Yu, Zhang Fei, and Liu Bei agains Cao Cao.
swap.answerHtml: Romance of the Three Kingdoms [or Chronicle of the Three Kingdoms; or Sānguó Yănyì; or Sānguó zhi Yănyì; or Sānguó Zhì]
swap.clue: Important weapons in this work include the Sword of the Seven Gems, and it features its central figures swearing on a Peach Tree while in a garden.

question.text: Tsai was a chief drafter of the special state-to-state relations doctrine pursued by this predecessor of Chen. Nicknamed "Mr. Democracy," this first directly elected President of Taiwan partially initiated the Third Taiwan Straits Crisis by making a 1995 visit to his alma mater, Cornell.
question.clue: In the 1980s, this person nicknamed "Mr. Democracy" asserted that his country's claims to the Spratly Islands were exactly the same as China's. This person's trip to his alma mater Cornell in 1995 precipitated a military standoff between China and the US.

swap.leadin: This dynasty carried on extensive border wars with the Song Dynasty, and had a two separate government systems for the nomadic tribes of the north and its Chinese subjects in the south.
swap.text: Name this dynasty of Khitans that was toppled by the Jurchen in 1125.
swap.clue: After the demise of this dynasty, Yelu Dashi fled to Central Asia and established a successor state.
